passage:
"I'm not going to Chaitanya's birthday," Pradeep announced, dropping his bag.
Amma looked up from the vegetables. "Since when?"
"Since today. He laughed when I missed the penalty. In front of everyone. He's a fake friend. Always has been."
"Always?"
"Always."
"The Chaitanya who sat with you every day when you broke your arm in Class 6?"
Pradeep paused. "That was ages ago."
"The one who shared his notes before the exams? Who came at midnight when Thatha was in hospital?"
"...He still laughed today."
"He did. That was mean, and you can tell him so. But is today the whole story of him?"
Pradeep kicked at the doormat. "It feels like it."

qa.q: When did Pradeep break his arm?
qa.a: In Class 6.

qa.q: Why does Pradeep call Chaitanya a fake friend who "always has been"?
qa.a: Today's laugh hurts and is the freshest memory, so it feels like the truth about Chaitanya and pushes years of kindness out of view.

qa.q: What does Amma suggest Pradeep can do about the laugh?
qa.a: Tell Chaitanya it was mean, rather than dropping the friendship, while remembering today isn't the whole story.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya feel if Pradeep skipped the birthday without a word?
qa.a: Chaitanya might be confused and hurt, perhaps without even realising how much the laugh stung.

grounding: It shows a teenager judging a long-time friend by the latest quarrel and forgetting years of kindness.

passage: Last month I almost blocked Sumit. We'd had a stupid fight over our chemistry project: he forgot the chart paper, I snapped, he snapped back, and he said I always act like the boss. That night all I could think was, "That's who Sumit really is. Careless and rude." I'm Mridul, and I've known Sumit since we were six. He taught me to ride a cycle. He stood up for me when some seniors mocked my stammer in Class 7. He once walked me home in the rain when I was sick. None of that came into my head that night, only the chart paper and "boss". My sister asked, "Is he really like that, or was he like that today?" It took me a week to answer.

qa.q: What did Sumit forget?
qa.a: The chart paper.

qa.q: Why did Mridul think that night that Sumit was "careless and rude"?
qa.a: Mridul felt angry after the fight, the most recent thing between them, so it seemed like the real Sumit, and years of kindness like the cycle and the stammer didn't come to mind.

qa.q: What does the sister's question help Mridul see?
qa.a: The difference between one bad day and who Sumit has been for years, so a single fight doesn't decide the whole friendship.

qa.q: What might Sumit have felt during that week?
qa.a: Sumit might have been hurt by the fight too, and unsure whether a friendship going back to age six was over.

grounding: It shows a teenager treating the latest fight as the truth about a friend and forgetting years of kindness.

passage:
Class teacher's note, 9B, Friday.
Shalini asked this morning to be moved away from Kavitha. They have sat together since Class 5. Yesterday they argued over a shared lunch box that was left open and ants got in; I heard raised voices. Shalini told me, "She's always been selfish, ma'am. I just didn't see it." When I asked for another example, she couldn't give one. Then she remembered, on her own, that Kavitha had brought her notes every day when she was ill for weeks last year, and she went quiet. I have not moved the seat yet. I suggested they each tell the other one thing they were upset about, with me nearby if they want. I'll check with both on Monday.

qa.q: How long have Shalini and Kavitha sat together?
qa.a: Since Class 5.

qa.q: Why does Shalini say Kavitha has "always been selfish"?
qa.a: Yesterday's argument is fresh and hurts, so it feels like the real Kavitha, even though Shalini can't name another example.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped, and why?
qa.a: Asking for another example let Shalini remember Kavitha's kindness on her own, and not moving the seat yet gave the friendship a chance.

qa.q: How might Kavitha feel if she learned Shalini wanted to change seats?
qa.a: Kavitha might feel shocked and hurt that one argument over a lunch box outweighed years of sitting together and bringing notes.

grounding: It shows a teenager judging a long-time friend by one recent quarrel and forgetting her past kindness.

passage:
Saturday night
Raghav and I are DONE. Today at the science exhibition he told Ma'am that the solar oven idea was his. It was OURS. I did the foil and the angles. He just stood there nodding while she praised him.
I told him in the corridor he's a selfish show-off. He said I'm "always so dramatic". So that's it. He's always been like this, I just never saw it.
Mumma said, "Raghav, beti? The boy who walked you home every day in Class 5 when you were scared of the dogs?" And that he gave me half his tiffin for a whole month when mine got stolen.
I know. But that was ages ago. Today is what he's REALLY like.
Deleting his number tomorrow.
— Vidya

qa.q: What did Raghav tell Ma'am at the science exhibition?
qa.a: He told Ma'am that the solar oven idea was his.

qa.q: Why does today's quarrel feel like the truth about Raghav to Vidya?
qa.a: Vidya is freshly hurt, so the latest event feels like his real character, and the years of walking home together and sharing tiffin seem like they no longer count.

qa.q: At which moment could Vidya choose differently, and what might she do?
qa.a: Before deleting his number tomorrow; she could wait a few days, think about the Class 5 walks and the shared tiffin, and then tell Raghav calmly that she wants credit for her part.

qa.q: How might Raghav be feeling after being called a selfish show-off?
qa.a: Raghav may feel stung and defensive, as his "dramatic" comeback suggests, and perhaps a bit guilty if he knows he took too much credit.

grounding: It shows a teenager judging a friend by the latest quarrel and forgetting years of kindness.

passage:
Nandini: I'm unfollowing Megha. seriously done
Sunaina: what happened??
Nandini: she didn't save me a seat at the fest today. sat with her new drama friends 😠
Nandini: that's who she is now. fake
Sunaina: nandini she's been your best friend since Class 2
Sunaina: she made that whole birthday video for you last month
Nandini: that was before
Sunaina: and when you broke your arm she brought notes every single day
Nandini: ok but TODAY showed me the real her
Sunaina: or today was one bad day? did you ask her why?
Nandini: why should I ask. she should know
Sunaina: 🤔
Nandini: I'm unfollowing her tonight

qa.q: What did Megha make for Nandini last month?
qa.a: She made that whole birthday video for Nandini last month.

qa.q: Why does Nandini feel today "showed the real" Megha?
qa.a: The seat at the fest is the newest and sharpest hurt, so it feels like Megha's true self, while years of friendship and kindness fade into "before".

qa.q: What could Nandini do before unfollowing Megha tonight?
qa.a: Take Sunaina's suggestion and ask Megha why she sat elsewhere, and think back to the birthday video and the daily notes before deciding who Megha is.

qa.q: How does Sunaina see the quarrel between Nandini and Megha?
qa.a: Sunaina sees it as possibly one bad day in a long, caring friendship, and wants Nandini to remember the notes and the video before cutting Megha off.

grounding: It shows a teenager judging a friend by the latest quarrel and forgetting years of kindness because the most recent event feels like the truth.
